jobs.description:
**Location**
: 100% Remote from India, min. 4h overlap with CET (e.g. 9:00–13:00 CET). Fluent English, spoken and written. German is not required.
  
  
**Compensation**
: 20k-32k USD per year (depending on location) + Shares + Generous Benefits. We pay local rates that are at or above the market. We share this philosophy with GitLab.
  
  
**About Secfix**
Secfix automates security compliance for SMBs and mid-market companies in Europe and gets them compliant with ISO 27001, GDPR, TISAX and SOC 2 in weeks instead of months. We’re a fast-growing team of 36 people, backed by a $12M Series A from Alstin Capital, Neosfer (Commerzbank) and Bayern Capital.
  
  
**About The Role**
You’ll be the
**first engineer dedicated to our go-to-market team**
. You build and own the backend systems our BDRs and AEs run on every day: data pipelines, integrations, internal services and AI agents. Today, everyone runs their own setup for data, outreach and communication. You’ll replace that with one central, reliable system that scales with us. This is a hands-on engineering role: you’ll write code (Python, SQL) every day, connect APIs and build data pipelines and AI workflows, not configure tools or run RevOps. You report to our Head of GTM, work closely with Sales and exchange with our Engineering team on architecture and best practices. We own products and outcomes, not Jira tickets.
  
  
**What You'll Do**

* Data pipelines: Design and build pipelines that pull account and contact data from multiple sources and APIs, clean, deduplicate and score it, and sync it to our CRM as the single source of truth.
* Data layer: Design the data model and central database behind our GTM, connecting CRM, outreach and product data.
* Integrations & services: Integrate internal and third-party tools via REST APIs and webhooks, and build small internal services and tools where off-the-shelf tools fall short.
* Signals & automation: Build signal detection, lead scoring and routing, and alerts that tell the right rep which account to call today and why.
* AI agents: Build AI-powered tools and agents that take repetitive work off our AEs, from research to proposals to CRM updates.
* Reliability: Deploy, schedule, monitor and maintain everything you build: error handling, retries, rate limits, logging and alerts when something breaks.
* Ownership end-to-end: Investigate problems, find the root cause, ship the fix and document it so nothing depends on one person.

Your success: reps spend less time on manual work and more time with customers, and more pipeline comes from systems that run reliably and are actually used.
  
  
**About You**
You’re a backend engineer who loves building things real people use every day, and curious about the business: why a customer buys, which signal means a company is ready. You build systems that run reliably at 10x volume, not one-off scripts.
  
  

* Recent graduate (0–2 years) in Computer Science or a related engineering field with a strong academic record.
* 1+ years of backend experience through your first full-time job or internships in a startup environment.
* Strong engineering fundamentals: solid Python (or another backend language), SQL and data modeling.
* Experience building and consuming REST APIs and working with webhooks.
* You know how to run code in production: Git, deployment, scheduling, testing, logging and debugging.
* You think in systems: you understand how components depend on each other and what breaks when you change one part.
* Hands-on experience with AI coding tools and LLM APIs (e.g. Claude Code or the Claude API).
* You’ve built and shipped real things (a feature, service, data pipeline or internal tool) and can show them.
* Smart, structured problem solver and fast learner: you pick up new tools on your own and bring complexity down.
* Independent, proactive and comfortable communicating remotely, especially in writing.

**Nice to have:**
Experience with a cloud platform (AWS or GCP), a data warehouse, a CRM and its API, or GTM tools like Clay.
  
  
You
**should not apply**
if:
  
  

* You need detailed tickets telling you what to build.
* You only want to write code and don’t care about business impact.
* You don’t want to test, monitor and maintain what you ship.
* You’d rather be led than lead your own projects.
* You don’t want to work closely with Sales and the people who use your tools.

**Interview Process**

* ~30 min – Introductory call with our Talent team
* Technical take home challenge (~8–10h, 7 days to submit)
* ~90 min – Interview incl. live coding with our Head of GTM
* Final interview with our co-founder and Head of GTM

**What we offer**

* Remote Work: 100% remote work with a virtual office in Gather.
* Competitive Salary: Industry-competitive local salaries. We pay local rates that are at or above the market. We share this philosophy with GitLab.
* Equity: Generous equity package – we’re all owners of Secfix and beneficiaries of our collective success.
* Holidays: 26 days holiday + local public holidays.
* Health Insurance: Comprehensive health coverage.
* Development Budget: €1,000 annual personal development budget.
* Workspace Budget: Remote workspace budget and access to co-working spaces.
* Annual Retreat: Annual retreat to build connections and inspire ideas (this year we’re headed to Alicante, Spain!).
* Tech Equipment: Latest tech equipment (MacBook, monitors, headphones).
* Company Events: Company-wide events to build relationships and have some fun!
* Mentorship: We are backed by top VCs and accelerators and have direct access to world-class mentors.

Our values: we are obsessed with our customers, we build smart, we create trust, we are hacky, we take ownership, and we are leaders of remote.
  
  
*We are an equal-opportunity employer and remote-only company. We work in sync using Gather as our virtual office and therefore cannot support 100% asynchronous work.*

jobs.description:
**Falcon**
is the optimizing just in time (JIT) compiler in Azul Platform Prime. It compiles hot Java bytecode into highly optimized machine code and delivers Java performance that standard JVMs do not reach. Falcon is built on LLVM.

  

We are looking for a
**Compiler Performance Engineer**
to make Falcon generate even faster code. This is not a compiler front end role and not a compiler built from scratch: the compiler exists, runs in production at large enterprises, and your job is to find where the generated code is slower than it should be and fix it in the optimizer and code generator.

  

You will join a distributed team of compiler experts and work on real workloads with direct, measurable impact on customer performance.

**What You Will Do (aka Responsibilities)**
  

  
* Analyze performance of Java benchmarks and customer workloads, find gaps in generated code and trace them to their root cause in the compiler
  
* Implement and improve optimizations in Falcon's middle end and back end: inlining, loop optimizations, vectorization, redundancy elimination, speculative optimizations and their interaction with the runtime
  
* Improve code generation for x86\_64 and AArch64
  
* Write tests and benchmarks that prove the improvement and protect it from regressions
  
* Contribute changes upstream to LLVM where it makes sense
  

  
**What You'll Bring (Experience, Skills)**
  

  
* 2+ years of professional experience in compilers, JIT compilers or low level performance engineering
  
* Strong C++ design and coding skills
  
* Solid understanding of compiler optimization theory: SSA, data flow analysis, loop transformations
  
* Ability to read assembly and reason about why one instruction sequence is faster than another
  

  
**Very Nice to Have**
  

  
* Experience with LLVM IR and LLVM optimization passes, or with another optimizing compiler such as HotSpot C2, Graal, GCC or V8
  
* Experience with profilers such as perf, VTune or async profiler
  
* Knowledge of x86\_64 and/or AArch64 microarchitecture
  
* Experience with Java, Scala or Kotlin, or with JVM internals
  
* MSc or PhD in Computer Science with a compiler or performance focus

Itron Resiliency Solutions is an innovative business unit within Itron focused on solving mission critical problems for utilities through software and AI. Resiliency Solutions offers unique, market leading solutions for front-line worker safety, storm response, excavation damage prevention, construction management, and many more. These software and AI solutions solve end-to-end challenges for the utilities that power our society and are used by the largest and most complex organizations in the world such as National Grid, Southern Company, and Exelon.

Itron Resiliency Solutions is a global, diverse team of builders and innovators who tackle previously impossible challenges for our customers. If you have a desire to challenge yourself, solve impactful problems, and work with a passionate and talented team, this is the place.

The Emergency Preparedness & Response (EP&R) team builds the systems that keep critical operations running when it matters most. When storms and severe weather threaten communities and infrastructure across the US, our platform enables customers to rapidly procure, mobilize, and manage the workforce needed to respond to and recover from storm damage — often under tight timelines and high-stakes conditions. We are looking for a Principal Engineer who is deeply hands-on, works backward from customer pain points and business needs, and measures success by impact rather than lines of code shipped. You will be the technical anchor of the team: a backend-heavy full-stack engineer who knows our systems inside and out, reasons rigorously about trade-offs, and raises the engineering bar for everyone around you while leading the team toward outcomes that genuinely matter.

**About the role**
------------------

We're hiring a Software Engineer in Bengaluru to build and run production services. You'll own features end to end — from understanding the problem to shipping, monitoring and fixing what you built — with growing independence and support from senior engineers.

Our India engineering team is taking full ownership of core products and growing quickly, including a ground-up rebuild of a customer-critical service. You'll work closely with senior engineers, your Engineering Manager, Product and Customer Support.

**What you'll own in your first year**
--------------------------------------

* **Own:** Own features and services end to end with speed and quality — build, test, release, monitor, fix.
* **Well-scoped problems, then bigger ones.** Start with clearly defined work and grow into breaking down ambiguous problems yourself.
* **Design.** Write design notes for your features and get them reviewed; contribute to larger designs led by senior engineers.
* **Quality.** Write tests, add observability, and take part in on-call so issues are caught before customers see them.
* **Customers.** Understand who uses what you build, and learn from support issues what to fix next.
* **Code reviews.** Give and receive thoughtful reviews, and help onboard engineers who join after you.

**What you must bring**
-----------------------

These are the bar. We can't teach them on the job.

* **Experience:** 1–4 years building production software. We level on demonstrated scope, not years alone.
* **You've shipped code that runs in production.** Features or services you built, released and supported — not only coursework or prototypes.
* **You are strong at problem solving.** You can take an unfamiliar, feature-sized problem, reason through it, and land on a simple, correct solution.
* **You work independently toward a clear goal.** Given a clear goal, you figure out the steps, unblock yourself, and ask for help at the right moments.

We care how you engineer more than which language you did it in.

**Technical background**
------------------------

You've built production software with a modern stack, such as:

* **Cloud:** hands-on with AWS — you've deployed and debugged services running on it.
* **Languages:** strong in at least one modern language such as Python, Java or JavaScript/TypeScript.
* **Frameworks:** modern service frameworks such as FastAPI, Node.js or equivalents.
* **Databases:** solid data modeling and query fundamentals — you can design a schema, use indexes well, and explain why a query is slow and how you'd fix it.
* **Fundamentals:** data structures, API design, and the basics of caching and concurrency.

Exact tools matter less than depth. Strong experience on an equivalent stack is welcome.

**What sets great candidates apart**
------------------------------------

* **Impact you can explain.** You can say what changed because of something you built — for users, performance or reliability.
* **One problem you went deep on.** A bug, a performance issue or a design where you dug past the surface to understand why.
* **Ownership beyond the ticket.** You've fixed what you shipped when it broke, and improved it after release without being asked.
* **Framework mindset:** You notice repeated code and turn it into something reusable.
* **Learning speed.** You've picked up a new domain, codebase or technology quickly and delivered in it.
* **Curiosity about the user.** You've asked why a requirement exists, or suggested a simpler way to solve the user's problem.

**What we look for in everyone we hire**
----------------------------------------

Whatever the role, we hire for six things.

* **Customer obsession.** You care who uses what you build and whether it actually helped them.
* **Impact over activity.** You measure success by outcomes, not tickets closed or lines written.
* **Honesty.** You're specific about your own part in team work, raise problems early, and say what didn't work.
* **Independence.** You don't wait to be told every next step. You figure things out with little hand-holding
